hunt.justification: The LiteLLM supply chain compromise allows for unauthenticated RCE and credential theft at scale. Verifying the integrity of Python environments is critical for preventing unauthorized cloud access.

scenario.summary: A barrage of critical vulnerabilities in October 2026 including PHP2Shell, Node2Shell, and GitLab RCE enabled unauthenticated remote code execution, while a supply-chain compromise of the LiteLLM package facilitated persistent credential theft. Attackers poisoned LiteLLM's PyPI and Docker distributions with a payload that hijacks Python startup via .pth files and establishes a remote access trojan (RAT).

meta.rationale: Focus on developers and CI/CD runners where LiteLLM is likely used. ephemeral build agents are high priority.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has installed a poisoned version of the LiteLLM library to establish persistence via Python startup files and exfiltrate host credentials.

hunt.name: LiteLLM Supply Chain Poisoning and Persistence
hunt.description: This hunt targets the Cybersecurity Black Week compromise of the LiteLLM library (v1.107.0). It follows a gated flow, starting with a lead query that identifies the malicious package installation in process history to capture activity on ephemeral hosts. If the lead is positive, the hunt fans out to find rare Python persistence (.pth files) and sensitive credential access across the fleet. An agent then correlates these signals to confirm a compromise and trigger containment.

config.scoping_notes: Focus on developers and CI/CD runners where LiteLLM is likely used. ephemeral build agents are high priority.
config.beyond_detection: A static rule for package versions is bypassed by renaming. This hunt uses prevalence counting across .pth files and correlates it with specific Python-based file access behavioral patterns, providing a cross-surface signal that simple version checks miss.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%pip%install%litellm%{{malicious_version}}%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%litellm-{{malicious_version}}%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify hosts that attempted to install the compromised version of LiteLLM, including ephemeral hosts.
config.expected_signal: Rows showing pip or python commands installing the malicious version. Silence means no recorded installation events in the window.

primitive_config.label: Detect malicious LiteLLM installation events
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%pip%install%litellm%{{malicious_version}}%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%litellm-{{malicious_version}}%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Rows showing pip or python commands installing the malicious version. Silence means no recorded installation events in the window.

config.objective: Identify hosts that have LiteLLM version 1.107.0 installation activity in their process logs.
config.description: Read only the lead query to confirm if any host is affected.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts with confirmed LiteLLM installation activity.
config.success_criteria: A verdict naming the affected hosts.

config.question: the agent confirms at least one host has activity relating to version 1.107.0 of LiteLLM
config.condition: the agent confirms at least one host has activity relating to version 1.107.0 of LiteLLM
config.description: Open the expensive behavioral queries only when the lead is real.

config.content: SELECT file_name, file_path, process_name, process_cmd_line, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.pth' AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%site-packages%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%dist-packages%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY file_name, file_path, process_name, process_cmd_line HAVING host_count < 5
config.description: Stack-count .pth file creations to find rare startup hijacks and attribute them to a process.
config.expected_signal: Rare .pth files created on one or two hosts. Persistent malicious startup files will stand out from common library files.

primitive_config.label: Rare .pth file persistence
primitive_config.content: SELECT file_name, file_path, process_name, process_cmd_line, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.pth' AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%site-packages%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%dist-packages%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY file_name, file_path, process_name, process_cmd_line HAVING host_count < 5
primitive_config.expected: Rare .pth files created on one or two hosts. Persistent malicious startup files will stand out from common library files.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, install_path FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) = 'litellm' AND package_version = '{{malicious_version}}' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Confirm if the malicious version is currently installed on any disk in the fleet.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, file_path, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id = 2 AND LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%python%' AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.aws/credentials' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.ssh/id_%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/config.json' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.dockercfg' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/.npmrc') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find Python processes reading sensitive local secret stores.
config.expected_signal: Reads of cloud or SSH credentials by a Python interpreter. Legitimate tools may exist, but those matching the scope hosts are high risk.

config.description: Verify behavioral findings and identify exposed secrets.
config.instructions: Review the identified .pth files and the Python processes that read sensitive files. Confirm if LiteLLM was the primary actor and determine which cloud or SSH credentials were leaked.
